Here’s a focused 3-week peaking block to taper volume, maintain intensity, and arrive fresh and confident on meet day. Assumes she’s healthy, has completed accumulation with specific work, and knows her recent estimated 1RMs. Use RPE to autoregulate. Full gym access.

Global structure
- Main lifts: Competition-style squat (low bar if used in meet), competition bench (paused), competition deadlift (her meet style).
- Intensity: Maintain/creep up to 88–95% singles while reducing total volume.
- Volume: Drop weekly (~60–65% of prior in Week 1, ~35–40% in Week 2, ~15–20% in Meet Week), mostly via fewer back-off sets and reduced accessories.
- Fatigue management: Longer rest periods, fewer accessories, strict technique, bar speed focus.
- Frequency: 4 sessions per week in Weeks 1–2; 2 sessions in Meet Week plus the meet.

Estimated 1RM calibration
- If needed, run a low-fatigue single at RPE 7.5–8 in Week 1 Day 1 for each lift to confirm current strength. Adjust %s accordingly.
- Notation: Use RPE targets alongside % as guidance. Where they conflict, judge by bar speed/RPE.

WEEK 1 (21–15 days out): Peak intensity introduction, volume drop
Goal: Touch heavy but submaximal singles (RPE 8–8.5), modest back-off volume at low to moderate stress. Accessories trimmed but still present for movement quality.

Day 1 – Squat focus
- Comp Squat
  - Work up to 1@88% (RPE ~8–8.5)
  - Back-off: 3×3@75% (RPE ~6.5–7), 3–4 min rest
- 2-ct Paused Squat: 2×2@70% (RPE 6–7), crisp positions
- Planks or Pallof press: 3×30–40s or 3×12/side
- Optional: Light calf raises or reverse sled 2×15 easy
Notes: Prioritize consistent depth, breathing/bracing, walkout discipline.

Day 2 – Bench focus
- Comp Bench (paused)
  - Work up to 1@87–90% (RPE 8–8.5)
  - Back-off: 4×2@77–80% (RPE 7), 2–3 min rest
- 2-ct Paused Bench or Spoto: 2×3@72–75% (RPE 6.5–7)
- Chest-supported row or cable row: 3×8 @ easy–moderate
- Triceps pressdown: 2×10 light–moderate
Notes: Practice press command pauses. No grinders.

Day 3 – Deadlift focus
- Comp Deadlift (her meet style: conv/sumo)
  - Work up to 1@88–90% (RPE 8–8.5)
  - Back-off: 3×2@77–80% (RPE 7)
- Pause Deadlift just off floor: 2×2@70% (RPE 6–6.5)
- Single-leg RDL: 2×6/side light
Notes: Perfect setup consistency. Keep bar path tight, avoid hitching.

Day 4 – Bench secondary + light squat tech
- Close-Grip or Comp Bench (paused)
  - 1@85–87% (RPE ~8)
  - Back-off: 3×3@72–75% (RPE 6.5–7)
- Light Comp Squat or High-Bar Tech: 3×3@60–65% (RPE 5–6) for groove
- Face pulls: 3×12 easy
- External rotations or band pull-aparts: 2×15

WEEK 2 (14–8 days out): Sharpening; further volume drop, maintain heavy singles
Goal: Keep skill with ~90–92% singles at RPE 8–8.5; minimal back-off volume. Accessories minimal.

Day 1 – Squat
- Comp Squat
  - Work up to 1@90–92% (RPE 8–8.5; bar speed clean)
  - Back-off: 2×2@72–75% (RPE 6.5) or 1×3 if fatigued
- Light Pause Squat: 1–2×2@65–70% (RPE 6)
- Easy core: 2×30s plank

Day 2 – Bench
- Comp Bench (paused)
  - Work up to 1@90–92% (RPE 8–8.5)
  - Back-off: 2×2@72–75% (RPE 6.5)
- Long-pause Bench (2–3s): 1–2×2@70% (RPE 6)
- Very light row: 2×8 easy

Day 3 – Deadlift
- Comp Deadlift
  - Work up to 1@90–92% (RPE 8–8.5; no slowdown)
  - Back-off: 1–2×2@72–75% (RPE 6.5)
- Technique pull from floor: 1×3@60–65%, speed focus

Day 4 – Bench touch-up + light squat groove
- Comp Bench (paused)
  - 1@87–90% (RPE ~8)
  - Back-off: 2×2@70–72%
- Very light Comp Squat: 2×2@55–60% (RPE 5)
- Shoulder health: band work 2×12

WEEK 3 (Meet week; 7–0 days out): Taper and taper-specific practice
Goal: Shed fatigue, keep neural readiness, finalize attempts. Sessions are short, nothing above RPE 7–7.5. No accessories beyond light prehab.

Day 1 (Mon or ~5–6 days out) – Opener rehearsal
- Comp Squat: 1@85% (RPE ~7), then 1@90% only if bar speed is snappy and it feels like RPE ≤7.5; stop if any grind
- Comp Bench (paused): 1@85% (RPE ~7); optional 1@88–90% if very fast
- Comp Deadlift: 1@85% (RPE ~7)
Notes: Full commands for squat and bench. Treat like a mini meet with full warm-ups.

Day 2 (Wed or ~3–4 days out) – Speed and confidence
- Comp Squat: 2×1@70–75% fast, perfect technique
- Comp Bench (paused): 3×1@70–75% fast
- Deadlift: 1–2×1@70–75% fast
Notes: Done in 30–40 minutes. Leave feeling better than you started.

Day 3 (Thu/Fri or ~1–2 days out) – Optional light bench only (if she likes staying sharp)
- Bench (paused): 3×1@60–65%, RPE 5
- Shoulder/band work: 2×12 easy
If she prefers full rest, skip this.

Meet Day (Sat/Sun)
- Dynamic warm-up, specific bar warm-ups. Use plan below for attempts.

Warm-ups (meet day guideline)
- Squat: bar×8–10; 25–30%×5; 40%×3; 55%×2; 65%×1; 75%×1; 85%×1; then open.
- Bench: bar×10–12; 30%×5; 45%×3; 60%×1–2; 70%×1; 80–85%×1; then open.
- Deadlift: bar drills (if allowed) or 40%×3; 55%×2; 65%×1; 75%×1; 85%×1; then open.
Keep jumps consistent; last warm-up 5–7 minutes before platform.

Attempt selection strategy
- Base on reliable recent training single (Week 1–2), not old PRs if fatigue/cloudy.
- Squat:
  - Opener: ~88–91% e1RM or a weight she can triple on any day (RPE 6.5–7.5). Goal: smoke it.
  - Second: 94–97% based on opener speed; if opener moves slower, go conservative.
  - Third: 100–103% for PR attempt if second was clean; otherwise 98–100% to secure total.
- Bench:
  - Opener: 88–90% (strict pause practice in training).
  - Second: 94–97%.
  - Third: 100–103% if second was smooth.
- Deadlift:
  - Opener: 88–90%.
  - Second: 95–98% guided by bar speed and need for total/placing.
  - Third: 100–105% as needed; deadlift is the place to stretch if the day is going well.
Use bar speed and RPE: if any second attempts feel ≥9 RPE or form degrades, cap the third at small PR or a repeat/2.5–5 kg jump.

Autoregulation and adjustments
- If any Week 1–2 single feels like RPE 9 or slows markedly, lower back-off volume further (reduce one set) and cap top singles at 87–90% the rest of that week.
- If she feels exceptionally fresh and fast in Week 2, keep % but do not add volume; small bump of 1–2% on that day only is fine.

Recovery and taper practices
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours; standardize bedtime/wake. Avoid new stimulants. Deload caffeine slightly midweek before meet if she runs high daily doses; then normal dose on meet day.
- Nutrition:
  - Weeks 1–2: Maintain bodyweight; keep carbs high around training (2–3 g/kg carbs in the 24 h around heavy sessions), protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, fats moderate.
  - Meet week: Slightly reduce training-day carbs since volume is low; day-before-meet eat familiar foods, sodium normal-to-high, hydrate to pale yellow urine. If cutting/weight class management is needed, implement only established, mild strategies—no last-minute drastic changes.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day baseline; +500–1000 ml on training days. Include electrolytes with long sessions.
- Soft tissue/mobility: Light daily movement, 5–10 minutes easy mobility. Avoid deep tissue work within 72 hours of meet; if needed, keep it gentle.
- RPE discipline: No grinders in Weeks 1–2; Week 3 nothing above RPE 7.5.

Technical and logistical prep
- Practice commands every comp bench and at least once weekly on squat in Weeks 1–3.
- Standardize footwear, belt, sleeves, wraps, chalk, ammonia (if used) in training; no changes on meet day.
- Pack list by 2–3 days out: equipment, snacks (salty carbs, easy protein), fluids, ID, attempt cards, headphones, charger.
- Plan warm-up timing: begin ~50–60 minutes before flight start; deadlift warm-ups start after bench flight begins.

Example daily warm-up (all days)
- 5 minutes easy bike/row, then
- Movement prep: hip airplanes, 90/90, ankle rocks, T-spine openers, band shoulder series (5–7 minutes total).
- Barbell-specific ramp-ups as listed; no fatiguing plyos or long circuits.

This 3-week peak strips fatigue while keeping heavy singles skill sharp. Keep communication tight, watch bar speeds, and protect meet week freshness above all.

Light touch-up drills (1–2 sets, RPE ≤5–6), Weeks 1–2 only
- Scap set + isometric: On the bench with empty bar, set scapulae (retract + depress), hold 5–6 seconds while breathing, then 3–5 paused reps with competition grip.
- Long-pause bench: 1×2 at ~60–65% focusing on scapular depression (don’t chase extra retraction during the pause).
- Band lat activation: Straight-arm pulldown 1×10 easy before bench to cue “lats to pockets,” not to fatigue.
- Wall scap retraction/depression drill: 1×6 slow reps pre-lift.

Avoid during peak
- New grip width, new arch strategy, or exaggerated retraction that lifts shoulders off the pad or narrows the bar path.
- Fatiguing accessory changes (heavy rows/pulls) to “fix” the cue right now.

Meet week
- No drills beyond normal warm-up. One or two empty-bar sets to “set and forget” the shoulders, then run standard warm-up.

Rule of thumb: If bar path is straight, touch point is consistent, and she’s not losing her upper back off the chest, keep the cue exactly as is. If the cue causes the bar to touch too high or elbows to tuck excessively, soften it to “down-and-back, stay long through the arms” without chasing any technical change beyond that.

Here’s a clear, low-stress meet-morning run sheet you can hand her. Adjust clock times to the published weigh-in and flight start.

Assumptions
- 2-hour weigh-in, Flight A, planned start 9:00.
- Openers pre-selected and written on attempt card; coach will submit.
- She’s not making a hard cut. If she is, keep the same flow but follow the cut/refeed plan you’ve used before.

Backwards plan from 9:00 start
- 7:00–7:20: Arrive, check in, rack heights, equipment check, weigh in.
- 7:20–7:40: Light snack + fluids, bathroom, find warm-up room, set up station.
- 7:40–8:00: Chill, put on sleeves/shoes later; start general warm-up ~60 min before first squat.
- 8:00–8:45: Squat barbell warm-ups (finish last warm-up 5–7 min before first attempt).
- 8:45–9:00: Opener ready, belt on, ammonia only if she already uses it (optional), headphones off, listen for name.

Meet-morning checklist
- Wake time: ~3.5–4.5 hours before lifting. Light 5–8 min walk, gentle mobility, shower if she likes.
- Breakfast (post-weigh-in if in a 2-hr weigh-in; earlier if 24-hr): familiar carbs + a little protein, low fat/fiber. Examples: 1–2 rice cakes with honey + small yogurt, or a banana + sports drink. Sip 300–500 ml electrolytes.
- Caffeine: Use her normal dose split: 1/2 dose 60–75 min before first squat warm-up, 1/2 dose between squat and bench. No new products.
- Fluids: Small sips to thirst; aim pale yellow urine; don’t over-chug right before attempts.
- Gear: Double-check belt, shoes, sleeves, wrist wraps, singlet, socks, chalk, ID, attempt cards, snacks.

Warm-up protocols and timing
Global pacing
- Start general warm-up 55–60 minutes before flight start.
- Begin barbell warm-ups ~40–45 minutes out.
- Hit last warm-up 5–7 minutes before your opener.
- Take 2–4 minutes between warm-up sets; slightly longer for final sets. Share racks smoothly.

General warm-up (8–10 minutes)
- 3–5 minutes easy walk or bike in the venue.
- Dynamic mobility: hips, ankles, T-spine, shoulders (5–6 minutes). Keep it light and familiar. No deep static stretching.

Squat warm-ups (example for ~150 kg e1RM; scale to her numbers)
Target opener: ~88–91% of e1RM that she can triple on any day. Keep it automatic.
- Bar x 8–10
- 25–30% x 5
- 45–50% x 3
- 60% x 2
- 72–75% x 1
- 82–85% x 1 (last warm-up)
- Opener: 88–91%
Timing: Start bar work ~40–45 min out. Last warm-up 5–7 min before her name is likely called. Coach confirms rack height on first warm-up set.

Bench warm-ups (paused; example for ~90 kg e1RM)
- Bar x 10–12
- 35% x 5 with pauses
- 50% x 3 paused
- 62–65% x 2 paused
- 72–75% x 1 paused
- 82–85% x 1 paused (last warm-up)
- Opener: 88–90%
Timing: Begin 8–10 minutes after her last squat attempt, or when bench warm-up room opens. Aim last warm-up 5–7 minutes pre-opener. Practice commands on every rep.

Deadlift warm-ups (example for ~170 kg e1RM; no bouncing)
- 40% x 3
- 55–60% x 2
- 70% x 1
- 80–85% x 1 (last warm-up)
- Opener: 88–90%
Timing: Start when her bench flight begins or ~20 minutes before her flight deadlifts begin, depending on meet flow. Fewer sets are fine; conserve energy.

Attempt selection and real-time adjustments
- Squat
  - Opener: 88–91% e1RM, smoke it (RPE 6.5–7.5).
  - Second: 94–97% guided by opener speed.
  - Third: 100–103% if second was clean; otherwise 98–100% to lock total.
- Bench
  - Opener: 88–90% (true pause).
  - Second: 94–97%.
  - Third: 100–103% if second was smooth.
- Deadlift
  - Opener: 88–90%.
  - Second: 95–98% based on need and speed.
  - Third: 100–105% as needed for PR/placing.

Speed-based guardrails
- If opener feels ≥8.5 RPE or visibly slows, pull back the second by 2.5–5 kg.
- If last warm-up feels off, lower the opener 2.5–5 kg. Better to build momentum.
- If she misses an opener on a non-strength issue (command, depth), repeat the same weight.

Between attempts
- Sit, breathe, small sips of sports drink, tiny bites of easy carbs (gummy bears, bites of banana), keep warm.
- Keep cues simple: one setup cue, one execution cue. No new tech talk.

Contingencies
- Flight runs fast: Trim one early warm-up set (e.g., drop the 45–50% on squat) and keep the last two singles.
- Flight runs slow: Add 2–3 very light “potentiation” singles at 40–50% spaced 6–8 minutes apart to stay warm.
- Shared rack limited: Bring change plates, be assertive but friendly, and keep her sequence simple.

Simple meet-morning timeline (9:00 start example)
- 6:00–6:30 Wake, light walk, shower
- 7:00 Arrive, weigh-in window opens; rack heights, equipment check
- 7:20–7:40 Snack + electrolytes, relax
- 8:00 General warm-up starts
- 8:15–8:45 Squat barbell warm-ups
- 8:53 In the on-deck area, belt on
- 9:00 Squat opener
- Post-squat: 10–15 min snack + sip fluids; begin bench warm-up on schedule
- Repeat flow for bench, then deadlift

Keep the day boring, predictable, and light. The win is calm, clean openers and controlled jumps.

Yes—insert a low-stress deload microcycle right after Week 1 to drop fatigue without losing the “heavy-singles” skill. We’ll turn the plan into a 3+1 structure: Week 1 (intro peak) → Deload (5–6 days) → Week 2 (sharpen) → Meet Week (taper). The deload removes almost all back-off volume, keeps bar speed snappy, and caps intensity at RPE ≤7.5. Accessories are minimal.

Overview of adjustments
- Total volume: ~20–30% of Week 1.
- Intensity: Keep to 70–82% on singles and doubles; no grinders.
- Frequency: 3 short sessions across the week (Squat/Bench, Deadlift/Bench, Optional light bench-only), each 25–45 minutes.
- Goal: Nervous system practice without accumulating fatigue; exit the week feeling better than you started.

Deload week (insert between original Week 1 and Week 2)
Day 1 – Squat + Bench (tech polish; RPE ≤7)
- Comp Squat
  - Ramp with small jumps to 2×1 at 78–82% (RPE ~6.5–7), full comp setup
  - Back-off: none or 1×2 at 65–70% if she wants groove work
- Comp Bench (paused)
  - Ramp to 2×1 at 75–80% (RPE ~6.5–7)
  - Back-off: none or 1×2 at 65–70% paused
- Optional accessories: band pull-aparts or face pulls 2×12 easy
- Notes: Longer rest, crisp walkouts, full pauses, no strain.

Day 2 – Deadlift + Bench (short, snappy; RPE ≤7)
- Comp Deadlift (meet style)
  - Ramp to 2×1 at 78–82% (RPE ~6.5–7)
  - Back-off: none
- Comp Bench (paused)
  - 2×1 at 75–80% (RPE ~6.5–7)
- Optional: 1×3 tempo RDL at 50–55% very light, or skip if any back fatigue
- Notes: Set up identically each rep, bar path tight, no hitching.

Day 3 – Optional bench-only primer (skip if any shoulder or systemic fatigue)
- Comp Bench (paused): 3×1 at 70–75% (RPE ~6), speed focus
- Shoulder health: band external rotations 2×12 easy
- Notes: This is purely for confidence and command practice.

Active recovery and cardio during deload
- Keep the easy “prep cardio” you added, but trim to 8–12 minutes/session, RPE 3 only.
- Gentle mobility 5–8 minutes daily. No deep tissue within 72 hours of resuming heavier work.

Then resume with the previously planned Week 2 and Meet Week exactly as written
- Week 2 (now 14–8 days out from meet) remains the “sharpening” week with 90–92% singles and very small back-off volume.
- Meet Week stays as the taper with opener rehearsal and speed day.

If you prefer to keep four training days in the deload
- Add a very light squat groove session: Comp Squat 2×2 at 55–60% (RPE 5) plus Bench 2×2 at 60–65% (paused), done in 20 minutes, placed 48 hours after Day 2.

Autoregulation guardrails for the deload
- If any single approaches RPE 8, stop there and end the lift; skip remaining singles.
- If she feels sluggish, extend the warm-up slightly and keep top singles at 75–78% only.
- Show up/leave rule: She should leave each session feeling better than when she arrived.

Nutrition and sleep in the deload
- Keep protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day. Carbs can dip slightly on non-lifting days but keep 1–1.5 g/kg around sessions to support neural pop.
- Prioritize 8+ hours sleep, consistent caffeine routines, and hydration with electrolytes.

This micro-deload preserves technical sharpness and heavy-singles rhythm while shedding the leftover accumulation fatigue, setting up a cleaner Week 2 and fresher meet day.

We can accommodate a controlled 95% single for each lift in Week 2 without compromising the taper. Key guardrails: cap at RPE 8.5, no grinders, and reduce or remove back-off work that day to keep total stress low. If bar speed isn’t there, cap at 92% and call it your opener rehearsal.

Where to place the 95% singles
- Week 2, mid-week, on the main lift days. Keep one lift per day at 95% to avoid stacking fatigue.
- Structure:
  - W2D1: Squat 95% single
  - W2D2: Bench 95% single
  - W2D3: Deadlift 95% single
  - W2D4: Bench touch-up (no 95%)

Updated Week 2 (14–8 days out)
Goal: Confirm opener readiness via clean 95% singles at RPE ≤8.5. Reduce back-off volume further to keep fatigue low.

Day 1 – Squat (95% single day)
- Comp Squat
  - Ramp with normal jumps
  - 1×1 @ 95% (RPE ≤8.5; must be clean and fast for the load)
  - Back-off: optional 1×2 @ 70–72% OR skip if any fatigue
- Light Pause Squat: skip this week
- Core: 1–2×20–30s easy plank (optional)

Day 2 – Bench (95% single day)
- Comp Bench (paused)
  - Ramp with full pauses
  - 1×1 @ 95% (RPE ≤8.5; strict pause)
  - Back-off: optional 1–2×1 @ 72–75% paused for groove OR skip
- Accessories: none

Day 3 – Deadlift (95% single day)
- Comp Deadlift
  - Ramp with standard jumps
  - 1×1 @ 95% (RPE ≤8.5; no sticking/hitching)
  - Back-off: none OR 1×1 @ 70% speed single if she wants to feel snappy
- Technique pull: skip

Day 4 – Bench touch-up + light squat groove (no heavy work)
- Comp Bench (paused): 2–3×1 @ 70–75% fast
- Very light Comp Squat: 2×2 @ 55–60% (RPE 5)
- Shoulder band work: 2×12 easy

Autoregulation and fallback rules
- If any top single feels ≥9 RPE or slows markedly, stop the set, log that weight as ~92–93%, and treat it as the opener rehearsal. Do not reattempt heavier.
- If squat 95% takes more than ~4 seconds concentric, cut all back-off work and trim next day’s bench by 2–3%.
- If deadlift 95% feels sticky off the floor, drop meet opener by 2.5–5 kg or keep the same opener and reduce second-attempt plan.

Placement relative to deload/Week 1 and Meet Week
- Keep the inserted deload exactly as planned between Week 1 and Week 2.
- Meet Week remains unchanged: opener rehearsal around 85–90% early week, then speed day. Do not chase 95% in meet week.

Warm-up guidance for 95% days
- Squat example progression: bar×8–10; 30%×5; 50%×3; 65%×2; 75%×1; 85%×1; 90%×1 (only if it’s snappy); 95%×1. Rest 3–5 minutes before the 95%.
- Bench: bar×12; 35%×5 paused; 55%×3 paused; 70%×2; 80%×1; 90%×1; 95%×1.
- Deadlift: 40%×3; 55–60%×2; 70%×1; 80–85%×1; 90%×1 (optional); 95%×1. Keep volume minimal, cues crisp.

Recovery that week
- Sleep 8+ hours, maintain carbs around those sessions (1.5–2 g/kg in the 24 h around each 95% day), keep easy cardio to 8–12 minutes max on non-95% days only.
- No new accessories; no heavy rows/RDLs.

Meet attempt planning linkage
- If 95% moves like an RPE ≤8, your opener can sit ~88–90% and second ~95–97%.
- If 95% is borderline, keep the opener conservative (86–88%), and make a smaller jump to the second.

This integrates the confidence-boosting heavy singles while protecting freshness for meet week.

Here’s a simple, repeatable 48-hour fueling plan to arrive topped off with glycogen, well-hydrated, and not bloated. Use only familiar foods. Adjust portions to body size and weight-class needs.

Targets
- Carbohydrates: ~4–6 g/kg/day 48–24 h out; ~3–5 g/kg day-before to morning-of. Favor low-fiber, low-fat sources.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day (normal). Keep portions moderate per meal.
- Fat: Lower than usual (roughly 20–25% of calories) to speed glycogen storage and reduce GI load.
- Fluids: 35–45 ml/kg/day baseline, plus 500–1000 ml around light sessions/travel. Sip steadily; avoid chugging.
- Sodium: Normal-to-high intake, 3–5 g/day total sodium (7.5–12.5 g salt), spread across meals and drinks. If she typically eats higher sodium, match her norm.

48–24 hours before (two days out)
- Goal: Top up glycogen without GI distress.
- Carbs: 4–6 g/kg across 4–6 meals/snacks. Examples per meal: white rice, potatoes, rice cakes, oats, sourdough, bananas, applesauce, pretzels, sports drink.
- Protein: Lean, familiar options (eggs/whites, chicken, turkey, low-fat dairy, whey).
- Fats: Keep servings small (e.g., 1–2 tsp oil or a small knob of butter if needed).
- Fiber: Moderate-low. Choose peeled fruit, cooked veggies (carrots, zucchini), small portions.
- Sample day:
  - Breakfast: Oats made with milk, banana, honey
  - Snack: Yogurt + granola + berries
  - Lunch: Chicken, white rice, soy sauce
  - Snack: Rice cakes + jam; sports drink
  - Dinner: Pasta with lean meat sauce; small salad cooked/soft veg
  - Pre-bed: Cereal with milk or chocolate milk
- Fluids: 35–45 ml/kg spread out + 500 ml electrolytes through the day.
- Sodium: Salt meals to taste; include soy sauce/broth/pretzels.

24–0 hours before (day-before and morning-of)
- Goal: Stay topped off, avoid bloat. Slightly reduce total volume of food vs. 48–24 h, keep carbs prominent.
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg in familiar, low-fiber forms.
- Protein: Normal.
- Fat: Low.
- Fiber: Low. Avoid big salads, beans, cruciferous veg, high-fiber bars.
- Day-before sample:
  - Breakfast: Toast with jam + eggs; orange juice
  - Snack: Rice cakes + honey; whey shake
  - Lunch: Turkey sandwich on sourdough + baked chips/pretzels; fruit cup
  - Snack: Applesauce pouch + sports drink
  - Dinner (earlier than usual): White rice or potatoes + lean protein + simple sauce; small cooked veg
  - Pre-bed: Cereal with milk or a small rice pudding
- Fluids: 35–45 ml/kg total. Include 500–750 ml electrolyte drink across the afternoon/evening. Stop heavy sipping 60–90 min before bed to protect sleep.
- Sodium: Keep normal-to-high. Salt meals; include a salty snack (pretzels/crackers) and/or a cup of miso/broth at dinner.

Morning of meet (2-hour weigh-in assumed; adjust if 24-hr)
- If not cutting: Light breakfast 2–3 h before lifting or post-weigh-in fueling if required.
- Immediate post-weigh-in (or upon arrival if no strict weigh-in timing):
  - 300–500 ml electrolyte drink (600–900 mg sodium/L) sipped over 20–30 min
  - 40–80 g fast carbs: banana + rice cakes with honey/jam, or sports drink + small yogurt
  - Keep fats minimal; avoid unfamiliar fiber.
- Between squat and bench, and bench and deadlift:
  - 20–40 g carbs per hour via sips/bites: sports drink, fruit snacks, gummy bears, bite-size bagels, applesauce. Small sips of electrolytes or lightly salted water.

Special considerations
- Weight class: If she needs to wake up a touch lighter, bias carbs/fluids earlier in the day-before and make dinner a bit smaller; keep sodium normal. After weigh-in, immediately rehydrate and eat as above.
- Caffeine: As usual—no new products. Split dosing as planned.
- GI comfort: Choose foods she’s used on heavy training days. Keep lactose low if sensitive.
- Signs to adjust: If urine is clear all day, you may be overhydrating—add electrolytes and reduce plain water. If waking up bloated, reduce dinner volume next time (more liquid carbs, fewer bulky solids).

Rule of thumb
- Familiar, simple, salty, and carby. Arrive neither stuffed nor hungry; steady sips, steady carbs.

Here’s the streamlined 3-week meet prep with the inserted deload, the 95% singles in Week 2, and the meet-day plan.

Structure at a glance
- Frequency: 4 sessions in Week 1, 3 short deload sessions, 4 sessions in Week 2 (with 95% singles), 2 sessions in Meet Week plus the meet.
- Volume: Steep taper across the block; accessories minimal and fade out by Meet Week.
- Intensity: Maintain heavy singles; cap fatigue (no grinders).

Week 1 (21–15 days out): Peak-intro, volume down, heavy-but-clean singles
- Day 1 Squat focus
  - Comp Squat: 1×1 @ ~88% (RPE 8–8.5), back-off 3×3 @ ~75%
  - 2-ct Paused Squat: 2×2 @ ~70%
  - Light core
- Day 2 Bench focus
  - Comp Bench (paused): 1×1 @ 87–90%, back-off 4×2 @ 77–80%
  - Paused/Spoto: 2×3 @ 72–75%
  - Light row + triceps (easy)
- Day 3 Deadlift focus
  - Comp Deadlift: 1×1 @ 88–90%, back-off 3×2 @ 77–80%
  - Pause DL: 2×2 @ ~70%
  - Light single-leg hinge
- Day 4 Bench secondary + light squat groove
  - Bench: 1×1 @ 85–87%, back-off 3×3 @ 72–75%
  - Squat technique: 3×3 @ 60–65%
  - Shoulder health band work

Deload microcycle (inserted between Week 1 and Week 2): 5–6 days, very low stress
- Day 1 Squat + Bench
  - Squat: 2×1 @ 78–82% (no back-off or 1×2 @ 65–70%)
  - Bench (paused): 2×1 @ 75–80% (no back-off or 1×2 @ 65–70%)
- Day 2 Deadlift + Bench
  - Deadlift: 2×1 @ 78–82% (no back-off)
  - Bench (paused): 2×1 @ 75–80%
- Day 3 Optional bench-only primer
  - Bench (paused): 3×1 @ 70–75% + easy band work
- Notes: Sessions 25–45 minutes, RPE ≤7. Keep easy cardio to 8–12 minutes max on non-lifting days.

Week 2 (14–8 days out): Sharpening with controlled 95% singles (one lift per day)
- Day 1 Squat (95% single)
  - Squat: Ramp to 1×1 @ 95% (RPE ≤8.5). Optional 1×2 @ 70–72% or skip.
- Day 2 Bench (95% single)
  - Bench (paused): 1×1 @ 95% (RPE ≤8.5). Optional 1–2×1 @ 72–75% paused or skip.
- Day 3 Deadlift (95% single)
  - Deadlift: 1×1 @ 95% (RPE ≤8.5). Optional 1×1 @ 70% speed or skip.
- Day 4 Bench touch-up + light squat
  - Bench (paused): 2–3×1 @ 70–75%
  - Squat: 2×2 @ 55–60%
- Guardrails: If any 95% looks ≥RPE 9 or grinds, cap there (call it opener rehearsal), cut all back-off, and trim next session by 2–3%.

Meet Week (7–0 days out): Taper and opener rehearsal
- Day 1 (Mon or ~5–6 days out) Opener rehearsal
  - Squat: 1×1 @ ~85% (optionally 90% if snappy, ≤RPE 7.5)
  - Bench (paused): 1×1 @ ~85% (optional 88–90%)
  - Deadlift: 1×1 @ ~85%
- Day 2 (Wed or ~3–4 days out) Speed/tech
  - Squat: 2×1 @ 70–75%
  - Bench (paused): 3×1 @ 70–75%
  - Deadlift: 1–2×1 @ 70–75%
- Day 3 (Thu/Fri or ~1–2 days out) Optional bench primer
  - Bench (paused): 3×1 @ 60–65% + light band work
- Meet Day: Standard warm-ups and attempt flow (below)

Meet-day plan (2-hour weigh-in assumed; adjust timing to schedule)
- Timeline example for 9:00 start
  - 7:00–7:20 Weigh-in, rack heights, equipment check
  - 7:20–7:40 Snack + electrolytes, set up in warm-up room
  - 8:00 General warm-up (8–10 min light movement/mobility)
  - 8:15–8:45 Barbell warm-ups; last warm-up 5–7 min before opener
  - 9:00 Squat opener
- Warm-up progressions (scale to her numbers)
  - Squat: bar×8–10; 30%×5; 50%×3; 60%×2; 72–75%×1; 82–85%×1 (last warm-up) → opener 88–91%
  - Bench (paused): bar×10–12; 35%×5; 50%×3; 62–65%×2; 72–75%×1; 82–85%×1 → opener 88–90%
  - Deadlift: 40%×3; 55–60%×2; 70%×1; 80–85%×1 → opener 88–90%
- Attempt selection
  - Squat: 1st 88–91%; 2nd 94–97%; 3rd 100–103% if 2nd was clean
  - Bench: 1st 88–90%; 2nd 94–97%; 3rd 100–103% if clean
  - Deadlift: 1st 88–90%; 2nd 95–98%; 3rd 100–105% as needed
  - If any second ≥RPE 9, cap third at small PR or secure total.
- Between attempts: Sit, breathe, small sips of electrolytes, 20–40 g carbs per hour in bites/sips; keep cues to one setup + one execution cue.

Recovery and support (brief)
- Easy “prep cardio”: 10–15 min easy walks/bike in Week 1; 8–12 min sessions during deload; 8–10 min light sessions in Meet Week on non-lifting days only.
- Sleep 8+ hours; protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg; carbs high around heavy days; meet-eve and morning fueling per 48-hour plan (simple, salty, carby; steady fluids/electrolytes).

This preserves heavy-single skill, drops volume and fatigue, confirms openers at 95% in Week 2, and lands her fresh and confident on the platform.

Here’s the streamlined 3-week meet prep with the inserted deload, the 95% singles in Week 2, and the meet-day plan.

Structure at a glance
- Frequency: 4 sessions in Week 1, 3 short deload sessions, 4 sessions in Week 2 (with 95% singles), 2 sessions in Meet Week plus the meet.
- Volume: Steep taper across the block; accessories minimal and fade out by Meet Week.
- Intensity: Maintain heavy singles; cap fatigue (no grinders).

Week 1 (21–15 days out): Peak-intro, volume down, heavy-but-clean singles
- Day 1 Squat focus
  - Comp Squat: 1×1 @ ~88% (RPE 8–8.5), back-off 3×3 @ ~75%
  - 2-ct Paused Squat: 2×2 @ ~70%
  - Light core
- Day 2 Bench focus
  - Comp Bench (paused): 1×1 @ 87–90%, back-off 4×2 @ 77–80%
  - Paused/Spoto: 2×3 @ 72–75%
  - Light row + triceps (easy)
- Day 3 Deadlift focus
  - Comp Deadlift: 1×1 @ 88–90%, back-off 3×2 @ 77–80%
  - Pause DL: 2×2 @ ~70%
  - Light single-leg hinge
- Day 4 Bench secondary + light squat groove
  - Bench: 1×1 @ 85–87%, back-off 3×3 @ 72–75%
  - Squat technique: 3×3 @ 60–65%
  - Shoulder health band work

Deload microcycle (inserted between Week 1 and Week 2): 5–6 days, very low stress
- Day 1 Squat + Bench
  - Squat: 2×1 @ 78–82% (no back-off or 1×2 @ 65–70%)
  - Bench (paused): 2×1 @ 75–80% (no back-off or 1×2 @ 65–70%)
- Day 2 Deadlift + Bench
  - Deadlift: 2×1 @ 78–82% (no back-off)
  - Bench (paused): 2×1 @ 75–80%
- Day 3 Optional bench-only primer
  - Bench (paused): 3×1 @ 70–75% + easy band work
- Notes: Sessions 25–45 minutes, RPE ≤7. Keep easy cardio to 8–12 minutes max on non-lifting days.

Week 2 (14–8 days out): Sharpening with controlled 95% singles (one lift per day)
- Day 1 Squat (95% single)
  - Squat: Ramp to 1×1 @ 95% (RPE ≤8.5). Optional 1×2 @ 70–72% or skip.
- Day 2 Bench (95% single)
  - Bench (paused): 1×1 @ 95% (RPE ≤8.5). Optional 1–2×1 @ 72–75% paused or skip.
- Day 3 Deadlift (95% single)
  - Deadlift: 1×1 @ 95% (RPE ≤8.5). Optional 1×1 @ 70% speed or skip.
- Day 4 Bench touch-up + light squat
  - Bench (paused): 2–3×1 @ 70–75%
  - Squat: 2×2 @ 55–60%
- Guardrails: If any 95% looks ≥RPE 9 or grinds, cap there (call it opener rehearsal), cut all back-off, and trim next session by 2–3%.

Meet Week (7–0 days out): Taper and opener rehearsal
- Day 1 (Mon or ~5–6 days out) Opener rehearsal
  - Squat: 1×1 @ ~85% (optionally 90% if snappy, ≤RPE 7.5)
  - Bench (paused): 1×1 @ ~85% (optional 88–90%)
  - Deadlift: 1×1 @ ~85%
- Day 2 (Wed or ~3–4 days out) Speed/tech
  - Squat: 2×1 @ 70–75%
  - Bench (paused): 3×1 @ 70–75%
  - Deadlift: 1–2×1 @ 70–75%
- Day 3 (Thu/Fri or ~1–2 days out) Optional bench primer
  - Bench (paused): 3×1 @ 60–65% + light band work

Meet-day plan (2-hour weigh-in assumed; adjust timing to schedule)
- Timeline example for 9:00 start
  - 7:00–7:20 Weigh-in, rack heights, equipment check
  - 7:20–7:40 Snack + electrolytes, set up in warm-up room
  - 8:00 General warm-up (8–10 min light movement/mobility)
  - 8:15–8:45 Barbell warm-ups; last warm-up 5–7 min before opener
  - 9:00 Squat opener
- Warm-up progressions (scale to her numbers)
  - Squat: bar×8–10; 30%×5; 50%×3; 60%×2; 72–75%×1; 82–85%×1 (last warm-up) → opener 88–91%
  - Bench (paused): bar×10–12; 35%×5; 50%×3; 62–65%×2; 72–75%×1; 82–85%×1 → opener 88–90%
  - Deadlift: 40%×3; 55–60%×2; 70%×1; 80–85%×1 → opener 88–90%
- Attempt selection
  - Squat: 1st 88–91%; 2nd 94–97%; 3rd 100–103% if 2nd was clean
  - Bench: 1st 88–90%; 2nd 94–97%; 3rd 100–103% if clean
  - Deadlift: 1st 88–90%; 2nd 95–98%; 3rd 100–105% as needed
  - If any second ≥RPE 9, cap third at small PR or secure total.
- Between attempts: Sit, breathe, small sips of electrolytes, 20–40 g carbs per hour in bites/sips; keep cues to one setup + one execution cue.

Recovery and support (brief)
- Easy “prep cardio”: 10–15 min easy walks/bike in Week 1; 8–12 min sessions during deload; 8–10 min light sessions in Meet Week on non-lifting days only.
- Sleep 8+ hours; protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg; carbs high around heavy days; meet-eve and morning fueling per 48-hour plan (simple, salty, carby; steady fluids/electrolytes).

This preserves heavy-single skill, drops volume and fatigue, confirms openers at 95% in Week 2, and lands her fresh and confident on the platform.
